rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentator says he received the report that Mary was permitted to make this declaration of silence.
rows.anchor: بلغني أنه أذن لها في هذا الكلام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Mary's abstention from speech was a sign God made for her then; he contrasts it with a foolish woman imitating her fast and silence.
rows.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: إنما كانت آية جعلها الله لها يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'you have brought' is glossed as 'you have come.'
rows.anchor: قالوا يا مريم لقد جئت} [مريم: 27] لقد أتيت

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda explain farī as something grave or tremendous.
rows.anchor: شيئا فريا} [مريم: 27] يعني عظيما في تفسير مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī glosses Mary's father's not being an evil man as his not being an adulterer.
rows.anchor: رجل سوء، يعني ما كان زانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's mother was not a prostitute or adulteress.
rows.anchor: وما كانت أمك بغيا} [مريم: 28] يعني وما كانت أمك زانية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda distinguishes this Aaron from Moses' brother: he was another Aaron, righteous and beloved among his clan.
rows.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: ليس بهارون أخي موسى ولكنه هارون آخر كان يسمى هارون الصالح

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A report says forty thousand Israelites, all named Aaron, followed the righteous Aaron's funeral.
rows.anchor: ذكر لنا أنه اتبع جنازته يوم مات أربعون ألفا كلهم يسمى هارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Mary Aaron's sister refers to her devotion and virtue.
rows.anchor: أي فقالوا: {يا أخت هارون} [مريم: 28] في عبادته وفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary gestured toward Jesus with her hand.
rows.anchor: قوله: {فأشارت إليه} [مريم: 29] بيدها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Mary was directing the people to speak to Jesus.
rows.anchor: بيدها. قال قتادة: أمرتهم بكلامه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī takes 'who was' as meaning 'who is he?'
rows.anchor: قالوا كيف نكلم من كان} [مريم: 29] يعني: من هو. تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the cradle as a stone lap or resting place.
rows.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: المهد، الحجر

rows.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
rows.claim: Some Kufans explain Jesus being blessed wherever he is as being a teacher and educator.
rows.anchor: سمعت بعض الكوفيين يقول: أي معلما، مؤدبا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains Jesus' dutifulness to his mother as obedience to Mary's command.
rows.anchor: أي: وجعلني برا بوالدتي، يعني مطيعا لأمر مريم. تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was not arrogant in worshipping God and was not wretched.
rows.anchor: {ولم يجعلني جبارا شقيا} [مريم: 32] مستكبرا عن عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Peace upon me' and the birth and death phrases refer to those times, while being raised alive refers to Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: {والسلام علي يوم} [مريم: 33] حين. {ولدت ويوم} [مريم: 33] وحين. {أموت ويوم أبعث حيا} [مريم: 33] يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus did not speak again after his infant declaration until he reached the age of boys.
rows.anchor: ولم يتكلم بعد ذلك بشيء حتى بلغ مبلغ الغلمان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the 'word of truth' is God Himself.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: والحق هو الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Jews and Christians disputed about Jesus: Jews called him a lying magician, while Christians claimed he was God's son, one of three, and a god.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: امترت فيه اليهود والنصارى. أما اليهود فزعموا أنه ساحر كذاب، وأما النصارى فزعموا أنه ابن الله وثالث ثلاثة وإله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God declares Himself exalted above what they say about Him.
rows.anchor: ينزه نفسه عما يقولون

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says God's decree that Jesus would be was already in His knowledge, although Jesus had no father.
rows.anchor: يعني عيسى كان في علمه أن يكون من غير أب. تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that God is Lord of Jesus and his audience, to be worshipped as the straight path, is Jesus' statement to them.
rows.anchor: هذا قول عيسى لهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the disputing parties as Christians divided over Jesus, and names their doctrines: the Nestorians made him God's son, the Jacobites identified him as God, and the Melkites said God is one of three, with Jesus and Mary as gods.
rows.anchor: هذا تفسير السدي. سعيد، عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا أن عيسى لما رفع انتخبت بنو إسرائيل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda recounts four Israelite jurists' positions after Jesus was raised: Jesus as God, God's son, a god with Mary and God, or God's servant and messenger; followers formed factions around the first three.
rows.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا أن عيسى لما رفع انتخبت بنو إسرائيل أربعة من فقهائهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: In the report, the fourth jurist says Jesus ate food while God does not, and the disputants acknowledge this argument.
rows.anchor: فقال المسلم: أنشدكم الله، هل تعلمون أن عيسى كان يطعم الطعام وأن الله لا يطعم الطعام؟

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Continuing Qatāda's account, the disputants acknowledge Jesus slept while God does not; the Muslim defeats them, the groups fight, and the Jacobites prevail as Muslims are killed.
rows.anchor: هل تعلمون أن عيسى كان ينام وأن الله لا ينام؟ قالوا: اللهم نعم. فخصمهم المسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The killing of those who enjoined justice is linked to the revelation of Qur'an 3:21.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تبارك وتعالى: {إن الذين يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the disbelievers witnessed a tremendous scene.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: شهدوا مشهدا عظيما

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the day people come to God as Resurrection Day and says their hearing and sight then are acute but too late to benefit them.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: وذلك يوم القيامة. قال: ما أسمعهم يومئذ وما أبصرهم. قال قتادة: سمعوا حين لم ينفعهم السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers in this passage are the polytheists.
rows.anchor: أي المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'clear misguidance' means plainly evident misguidance.
rows.anchor: اليوم في ضلال مبين} [مريم: 38] بين

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd describes the Day of Regret: every person sees a home in both Paradise and Hell, and the lost homes make each group regret its fate.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الزعراء، عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه ذكر حديثا في البعث قال: فليس من نفس إلا وهي تنظر إلى بيت

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains the settled matter as the punishment becoming due and the people of Hell falling into it.
rows.anchor: يعني إذ وجب العذاب فوقع أهل النار. تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report from Abū Saʿīd says death appears as a speckled ram, is slaughtered between Paradise and Hell, and both groups are told they will live forever without death.
rows.anchor: بلغني عن الأعمش، عن أبي سفيان، عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: يجاء بالموت في صورة كبش أملح

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that when the people of Paradise and Hell are admitted, death is slaughtered before them and they are told there is no more death.
rows.anchor: إبراهيم بن محمد، عن شريك بن أبي نمر، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي عمرة، عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says a caller announces to both groups that there is no death and each person remains forever in his state.
rows.anchor: عثمان، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر قال: سمعت رسول الله يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people in heedlessness are the polytheists living in this world; the statement looks ahead to their fate.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا. وهذا كلام مستقبل، يعني المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's inheriting the earth and everyone on it means He will destroy them all; everyone returns to Him on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: قوله: {إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها} [مريم: 40] نهلك الأرض ومن عليها.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says to recount Abraham's story to the people of Mecca, meaning to recite it to them.
rows.anchor: وهو تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's father worshipped idols that neither hear nor see nor benefit anyone.
rows.anchor: يعني الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge that came to Abraham means prophethood, and the straight path he offers is an upright religion, Islam, leading to Paradise.
rows.anchor: يعني النبوة. {فاتبعني أهدك صراطا سويا} [مريم: 43] يعني دينا عدلا، وهو الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping idols is worshipping Satan: the idols do not invite worship of themselves, but Satan calls people to it; the commentator connects this with Qur'an 4:117.
rows.anchor: إن عبادة الوثن عبادة الشيطان، لأن الوثن لم يدعه إلى عبادة نفسه ولكن الشيطان دعاه إلى عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says repentance remains acceptable until punishment descends; he hoped his father would repent, but that hope ended when he died in unbelief.
rows.anchor: وما لم ينزل العذاب فتوبتك مقبولة إن تبت. وقد كان إبراهيم يرجو أن يتوب. فلما مات على الكفر ذهب ذلك الرجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's father asks whether he rejects his gods by refusing to worship them.
rows.anchor: أن تعبدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat to stone Abraham means to kill him with stones if he stops insulting and denouncing the idols.
rows.anchor: لأرجمنك} [مريم: 46] بالحجارة فلأقتلنك بها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī instead explains the threat of stoning as a threat to insult Abraham.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {لأرجمنك} [مريم: 46] يعني لأشتمنك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses 'leave me for a while' as leave me safe.
rows.anchor: نا يحيى قال: نا سعيد، عن قتادة قال: واهجرني سالما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the requested separation as lasting for a time.
rows.anchor: نا يحيى، قال: نا عاصم بن حكيم أن مجاهدا قال: واهجرني حينا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, in a report from Qatāda, takes the separation to be for a long time.
rows.anchor: نا يحيى قال: نا سعيد، عن قتادة، عن الحسن قال: واهجرني طويلا

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Yaḥyā summarizes the meaning as prolonging Abraham's estrangement.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى: أي وأطل هجراني

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī interprets Abraham's greeting to his father as returning a good response.
rows.anchor: يعني رد خيرا في تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan calls Abraham's 'peace be upon you' a word of forbearance.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: وهذه كلمة حلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains God's being attentive to Abraham as answering his prayer rather than rejecting it.
rows.anchor: بدعائي فلا يرده علي في تفسير الحسن

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses God's care for Abraham as mercy.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير الكلبي: إنه كان بي رحيما

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some explain God's care for Abraham as gentleness.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: لطيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's promised request for forgiveness is linked to Qur'an 9:114, which says he had promised his father this.
rows.anchor: فهو قوله: {وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لأبيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه} [التوبة: 114]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects Abraham and his people worship besides God are their idols.
rows.anchor: يعني أصنامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham hopes that praying to his Lord will make him happy rather than wretched.
rows.anchor: أي عسى أن أسعد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The things Abraham left behind were his people's idols.
rows.anchor: يعني أصنامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three made prophets are Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
rows.anchor: أي إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy granted to them means prophethood.
rows.anchor: من رحمتنا} [مريم: 50] النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their elevated good repute means later generations follow their example and praise them; God preserved their good mention, as in Qur'an 26:84, 37:78, and 29:27.
rows.anchor: رفيعا، سنة يقتدي بهم من بعدهم وثناء عليهم من بعدهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says to recount Moses' story to the people of Mecca, meaning to recite it to them.
rows.anchor: وهو تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right side is the right side of the mountain; the passage is linked to God's call to Moses at the fire in Qur'an 20:11-12.
rows.anchor: أيمن الجبل، وهو قوله: {فلما أتاها نودي يا موسى {11} إني أنا ربك} [طه: 11-12]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drew Moses near when He spoke with him.
rows.anchor: حين كلمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Aaron Moses' minister and joined him with Moses in the mission.
rows.anchor: جعله الله له وزيرا وأشركه معه في الرسالة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says to recount the story of Ishmael son of Abraham to the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: يقول: اذكر لأهل مكة أمر إسماعيل بن إبراهيم. وهو تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: أبان العطار
rows.claim: Abān al-ʿAṭṭār reports that Ishmael kept a promised appointment for a year after the man failed to arrive.
rows.anchor: حدثني أبان العطار أن إسماعيل وعد رجلا موعدا فجاء الموعد فلم يجد الرجل، فأقام في ذلك الموضع حولا ينتظره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people whom Ishmael commanded to pray and give alms were his own people.
rows.anchor: وأهله: قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being accepted means God was pleased with him.
rows.anchor: قد رضي عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to mention Idris means to tell his story to the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: يقول: اذكره لأهل مكة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Idris was raised to the fourth heaven.
rows.anchor: نا يحيى، قال: نا سعيد، عن قتادة قال: في السماء الرابعة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says Idris did not die but was raised as Jesus was raised.
rows.anchor: قال: نا عاصم بن حكيم أن مجاهدا قال: لم يمت، رفع كما رفع عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets mentioned from the beginning of the chapter through this point are those God favored with prophethood.
rows.anchor: أنعم الله عليهم بالنبوة، يعني من ذكر منهم من أول السورة إلى هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions of Noah's ark were Noah's descendants; Idris descended from Adam before Noah, while Abraham descended from Noah.
rows.anchor: ذرية من كان في السفينة مع نوح. كان إدريس من ولد آدم قبل نوح، وكان إبراهيم من ذرية نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel is Jacob, whose descendants include those mentioned here; those guided are guided to faith.
rows.anchor: قال: {وممن هدينا} [مريم: 58] للإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's choosing means choosing or selecting through prophethood.
rows.anchor: بالنبوة. وتفسير اجتبينا اخترنا، وهو أيضا اصطفينا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the generation that followed the favored prophets as the Jews.
rows.anchor: حدثنا يحيى قال: نا سعيد، عن قتادة قال: اليهود

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Yaḥyā connects following desires to the Jews' marrying their nieces, citing Qur'an 4:27.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى: وقال في سورة النساء: {ويريد الذين يتبعون الشهوات أن تميلوا ميلا عظيما} [النساء: 27] اليهود في نكاح بنات الأخ

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd explains 'ghayy' as a valley of boiling water in Hell.
rows.anchor: حدثني شريك، عن أبي إسحاق الهمذاني، عن أبي عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود، عن أبيه قال: وادي في جهنم من حميم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Masʿūd describes ghayy as a deep-bottomed valley with foul taste in Hell.
rows.anchor: حدثني نصر بن طريف، عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي عبيدة، عن ابن مسعود قال: وادي في جهنم بعيد القعر خبيث الطعم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A further report from Ibn Masʿūd calls ghayy a river of the Fire's inhabitants' pus.
rows.anchor: نا يونس بن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي عبيدة، عن ابن مسعود قال: نهر في جهنم من صديد أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repent, believe, and act righteously lose none of their good deeds.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا ينقصون شيئا من حسناتهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says nothing will be deducted from their deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: من أعمالهم شيئا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains ʿAdn as the inner parts of Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: عدن بطنان الجنة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib describes the Garden of ʿAdn as containing God's footrest and the place of His Throne.
rows.anchor: عن يحيى بن سعيد، عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: جنة عدن التي بها موطأ الرب وموضع عرشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaḥyā says he received the report that the other gardens are named in relation to ʿAdn.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى: بلغني أن الجنان تنسب إليها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says ʿAdn is one of Paradise's names.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: عدن اسم من أسماء الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promised His servants Paradise in the worldly life for the afterlife, which is the unseen in al-Hasan's view.
rows.anchor: وعدهم في الدنيا الجنة في الآخرة. والغيب الآخرة في قول الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says belief in the unseen includes resurrection, reckoning, Paradise, and Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد عن قتادة في قوله: {يؤمنون بالغيب} [البقرة: 3] ، قال: بالبعث، وبالحساب وبالجنة والنار

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the speech absent from Paradise as lies, falsehood, or disobedience, treating these as equivalent descriptions.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم: كذبا. وقال بعضهم: باطلا. وقال بعضهم: معصية. وهو نحو واحد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains the prohibited talk as oaths like those made by worldly people when they drink wine.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: حلفا كفعل أهل الدنيا إذا شربوا الخمر

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the exception of peace as all good things.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم: إلا خيرا. وهو تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the people of Paradise greet one another.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: يسلم بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Paradise's people receive provision every hour; morning and evening are two hours within a day there, which has only light and no night.
rows.anchor: نا سعيد، عن قتادة قال: ولهم رزقهم فيها كل ساعة، والبكرة والعشي ساعتان من الساعات وليس ثم ليل إنما هو ضوء ونور

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says there is no morning in Paradise; people receive what they used to desire in worldly life.
rows.anchor: نا سفيان الثوري، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد قال: ليس فيها بكرة ولكن يؤتون به على ما كانوا يشتهون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaḥyā says he was told that residents receive breakfast three hours after the day begins and supper with three hours left, with a twelve-hour day like a worldly day.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى: بلغني أنه إذا مضى ثلاث ساعات أوتوا بغدائهم، فإذا بقيت ثلاث ساعات أوتوا بعشائهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet through Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says Paradise is shining white, its people are white, and they do not sleep or experience sun, dark night, harmful heat, or cold.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الجنة بيضاء تتلألأ وأهلها بيض

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
rows.claim: The Prophet answers that Paradise has no darkness or night; its trees, rivers, fruit, and servants are all light.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله أفي الجنة ليل؟ فقال: «إنه ليس في الجنة ظلمة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says the lowest entrant, marked by a scorch, receives a vast realm reaching a hundred years of sight, with abundant palaces, tents, family, servants, and plentiful varied meals that can feed all people and jinn without depletion.
rows.anchor: نا خالد، عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
rows.claim: A Prophetic report describes the lowest level of Paradise with seventy thousand attendants, each carrying a golden platter of different food whose first and last tastes remain delightful.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن سابط أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «والذي نفسي بيده إن أسفل أهل الجنة درجة

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
rows.claim: Continuing the Paradise report, the highest-ranking person is served by seven hundred thousand attendants with distinct foods; even the lowest resident surveys a thousand-year realm of pearl and ruby palaces, rivers, and hanging fruit.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: " ألا تسألوني عن أرفع أهل الجنة درجة؟ قالوا: بلى.

rows.speaker: الخليل بن مرة
rows.claim: A report says God admits people to Paradise through His mercy and apportions it to them according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: حدثني الخليل بن مرة أن الله تبارك وتعالى قال: «ادخلوا الجنة برحمتي واقتسموها بأعمالكم»

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the statement about descending only by the Lord's command is Gabriel speaking; after a pause in revelation, Gabriel tells the Prophet that the affairs ahead belong to God and means the afterlife.
rows.anchor: سعيد عن قتادة قال: هذا قول جبريل. احتبس عن النبي في بعض الوحي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī interprets what lies behind the angels as worldly affairs, in the circumstance of being in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وما خلفنا} [مريم: 64] من أمر الدنيا، وهو تفسير السدي، أي إذا كنا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What lies between the two is the affairs of this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وما بين ذلك} [مريم: 64] من أمر الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the interval between as the barzakh between the two trumpet blasts.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هو البرزخ، يعني: ما بين النفختين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī reads what is before and behind us as what preceded our creation and what comes after it.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا} [مريم: 64] يعني ما كان قبل خلقنا وما يكون بعد خلقنا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan connects perseverance in worship to what God has prescribed for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: لما فرض عليك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets whether God has a namesake as asking whether He has an equal.
rows.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: هل تعلم له عدلا

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Yaḥyā explains the question through the idea of being comparable or sharing a rank.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى: أي من قبل المساماة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the names Allah and al-Raḥmān are reserved names no creature could claim for itself.
rows.anchor: أبو الأشهب، عن الحسن قال: الله والرحمن اسمان ممنوعان لم يستطع أحد من الخلق أن ينتحلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question means that no one knows of any namesake equal to God.
rows.anchor: على الاستفهام، أي إنك لا تعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier of resurrection is identified as a polytheist; reports say Ubayy ibn Khalaf challenged the Prophet while crumbling a rotten bone and asking if God could revive it.
rows.anchor: هذا المشرك يكذب بالبعث وقد ذكروا أنه قول أبي بن خلف للنبي عليه السلام حيث جاء بعظم نخر ففته بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God created the person from nothing, He is able to resurrect him on the Last Day.
rows.anchor: فالذي خلقه ولم يك شيئا قادر على أن يبعثه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears to gather the polytheists together with the devils who invited them to worship idols.
rows.anchor: {فوربك لنحشرنهم} [مريم: 68] يعني المشركين. {والشياطين} [مريم: 68] الذين دعتهم إلى عبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says those gathered around Hell will be on their knees; Yaḥyā adds this is before they enter it.
rows.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: على ركبهم. قال يحيى: وهذا قبل دخولهم النار

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret 'juthiyyan' as groups gathered together.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {جثيا} [مريم: 68] جماعة جماعة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the people are assembled group by group, each nation separately.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: جماعة، كل أمة على حدتها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī interprets each sect as each community of religion.
rows.anchor: تفسير السدي، يعني من كل أهل ملة

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujāhid take each sect to mean each nation, and al-Hasan specifies its unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: من كل أمة. قال الحسن: يعني كفارها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the greatest insolence toward the Merciful means disbelief.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: كفرا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains the insolence as severity of hardness or callousness.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: شدة في القسوة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets the greatest insolence as the gravest disobedience.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: أشد معصية

rows.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: A report says a neck of Fire is assigned to seize those who associate another god with God or claim He has a child, and later those who curse, lie about, or harm God; it identifies the groups as child-claimers, resurrection-deniers, and image-makers, citing 40:16-17, 112:3-4, and 16:38-39.
rows.anchor: أخبرني رجل من أهل الكوفة، عن ليث، عن شهر بن حوشب قال: إذا كان يوم القيامة نزل الجبار تبارك وتعالى

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report from Abū Saʿīd says a neck of Fire is unleashed against every obstinate tyrant, swallows them, and returns after throwing them into Hell.
rows.anchor: المعلى بن هلال، عن الأعمش، عن عطية العوفي، عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: تندلق عنق من النار

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Yaḥyā says, as he recalls it, that the previous report mentioned two of the same traits.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى: فذكر خصلتين من الخصال التي في الحديث الأول فيما أحسب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says a neck of Fire is assigned to three groups: those denying God by rejecting messengers and scriptures, those falsely claiming He has a son, and image-makers who harm God.
rows.anchor: محمد بن راشد قال: سمعت قتادة يقول: تنزل عنق من النار فتقول: إني أمرت بثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who are most entitled to the Fire are those who enter it; some say the phrase means those punished most severely.
rows.anchor: يعني الذين يصلونها. وقال بعضهم: أشد عذابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that everyone will come to the Fire is expressed as an inevitable oath.
rows.anchor: يعني قسما كائنا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd describes the crossing as a sword-edged bridge over Hell, where angels with iron hooks catch fallers; the faithful cross at speeds compared to lightning, wind, fine horses, and strong beasts, while angels pray for safety.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله: {وإن منكم إلا واردها} [مريم: 71] قال: الصراط على جهنم مثل حد السيف

rows.speaker: نافع بن الأزرق
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq says unbelievers enter the Fire but believers do not.
rows.anchor: فقال نافع: أما الكفار فإنهم يردونها. وأما المؤمنون فإنهم لا يردونها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās rejects Nāfiʿ's exclusion of believers, saying he and Iyās will come to the Fire and see whether they emerge.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وعنده إياس بن مضرب، فقال ابن عباس: أما أنا وإياس فإنا سنردها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes the phrase to mean everyone enters the Fire, which God then makes cool and safe for believers as He did for Abraham.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال: {وإن منكم إلا واردها} [مريم: 71] إلا داخلها فيجعلها الله على المؤمن بردا وسلاما

rows.speaker: حفصة
rows.claim: When the Prophet hopes that participants at Badr and al-Ḥudaybiya will not enter Hell, Ḥafṣa objects by citing this verse; he answers by citing God's promise to rescue the God-fearing in 19:72.
rows.anchor: الحسن بن دينار، عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إني لأرجو إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A second report from Jābir transmits the same exchange about the Prophet's hope for Badr and al-Ḥudaybiya participants and the promise to rescue the pious.
rows.anchor: خالد، عن الحسن، عن جابر بن عبد الله، عن النبي نحوه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda explains the wrongdoers left in Hell as crouching on their knees.
rows.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: على ركبهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the wrongdoers remain in Hell in groups, one after another.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: جماعة جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers' question about which party is better means themselves or the believers.
rows.anchor: نحن وأنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two terms mean dwelling place and gathering place; Qatāda says the latter is a meeting council, essentially the same meaning.
rows.anchor: المقام: المسكن، والندي: المجمع. وقال قتادة: الندي، المجلس. وهو واحد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the polytheists of Quraysh address the Prophet's companions with this boast.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: يقوله مشركو قريش لهؤلاء أصحاب محمد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the Meccans saw the Prophet's companions living in hardship.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد: قال قتادة: رأوا أصحاب نبي الله في عيشهم خشونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier generations destroyed by God had more furnishings and a finer outward appearance than the current claimants.
rows.anchor: قال الله: {وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا} [مريم: 74] منهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athāth means wealth; another view takes it as household goods or possessions.
rows.anchor: والأثاث: المال. وقال بعضهم: المتاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the hamzated reading, ruʾyan means appearance; Qatāda glosses it as more goods and a better look, while al-Hasan says forms or images.
rows.anchor: {ورئيا} [مريم: 74] من قرأها مهموزة فيقول: منظرا. سعيد، عن قتادة قال: {أحسن أثاثا ورئيا} [مريم: 74] أكثر متاعا وأحسن مرآة ومنظرا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without hamza, the word derives from good appearance; people's livelihood depends on rain, which grows crops and sustains livestock.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأها بغير همزة فيقول: وريا من قبل الرواء. وإنما عيش الناس بالمطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person in misguidance is one who dies while remaining astray.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي يموت على ضلالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command for the Prophet to ask that the Merciful extend the misguided is a supplication for their extension.
rows.anchor: هذا دعاء، فأمد له الرحمن مدا. أمر الله النبي أن يدعو بهذا

rows.speaker: ابن مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Mujāhid, from his father, interprets the phrase as God leaving the misguided to their rebellion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مجاهد عن أبيه: فليدعه الرحمن في طغيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised punishment may be a worldly punishment before the final punishment.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا قبل عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour refers to the punishment of the afterlife, the greater punishment; every prophet warned his people of both worldly and afterlife punishment if they disbelieved.
rows.anchor: أي وإما عذاب الآخرة، فهو العذاب الأكبر. لم يبعث الله نبيا إلا وهو يحذر أمته عذاب الله في الدنيا وعذابه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the promise arrives, they will learn which party is worse situated, the unbelievers or believers.
rows.anchor: عند ذلك. {من هو شر مكانا} [مريم: 75] أهم أم المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having the weaker force means having no one to protect them from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: في النصرة والمنعة. أي إنهم ليس لهم أحد يمنعهم من عذاب الله

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains God's increase in guidance for the guided as an increase in faith.
rows.anchor: يعني: يزيدهم إيمانا. وهو تفسير السدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the enduring righteous deeds as the obligatory religious duties.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: الفرائض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the enduring deeds as the five prayers and the repeated praises: glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الصلوات الخمس، وسبحان الله، والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
rows.claim: A report says Abraham told the Prophet during the Night Journey to greet the community and tell them Paradise has good soil and water, lies level, and is planted through these four remembrance formulas.
rows.anchor: عن العلاء بن عبد الكريم، عن عبد الرحمن بن سابط قال: لما أسري بالنبي لقي إبراهيم النبي فقال له

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib gives the four remembrance formulas as the enduring righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: وحدثني أبو الأسحم عقبة بن مرثد، عن أبي إسحاق الهمذاني قال: سمعت علي بن أبي طالب يقول: الباقيات الصالحات

rows.speaker: محمد بن عجلان
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls the four remembrance formulas a shield from Hell; they will come on Judgment Day ahead, alongside, and behind their reciters as the enduring righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن عجلان أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأصحابه يوما: «خذوا جنتكم»
